analysis.title: The Day Ahead - North America, Monday, November 2, 2026
key_insights: Stocks fell sharply in the last session. The S&P 500 lost 1.82% to 7,580.07, the Nasdaq Composite lost 2.86% to 25,437.00 (its largest one-day percentage drop since June 5), and the Dow lost 1.09% to 51,770.31. The Nasdaq fell 5.3% in October and 2% for the week.

Amazon's AI spending plans and Intel's results drove the selloff. Investors are questioning the cost of the AI buildout and how fast it returns money. A Wealthspire strategist said the week has been about whether AI will earn a positive return on investment and how quickly.

Intel guided quarterly revenue more than $1 billion below market estimates and said it does not expect positive cash flow this year. The stock had its worst day ever and set off a global chip selloff. Weak PC demand and memory prices rising on AI demand were cited as pressures on device makers.

Meta, Alphabet and Amazon raised spending forecasts, turning once lightly indebted tech giants into heavy spenders reliant on borrowing. More than $2 trillion of Nasdaq 100 market value is set to be wiped out in October, with the index down over 5.8% for the month. Big Tech returned the smallest share of cash to shareholders in at least 15 years as AI spending squeezed buybacks.

Treasuries rallied as tech stocks fell. The 10-year yield was about 4.92%, the 2-year about 4.59% and the 30-year about 5.31%. A TD Securities strategist described a sentiment shift over the last few weeks, from viewing everything as an upside risk to rates to risks re-emerging on the other side. Earlier yields had hit multi-decade highs on energy costs and government debt.

The dollar index fell 0.13% to 101.90. The yen strengthened after the Bank of Japan left rates unchanged and raised its inflation outlook. An FXStreet analyst said the market was a little disappointed in the BOJ and that the Fed bias still counters it. Dollar/yen was 157.50.

Oil rose on expectations of an escalation in the Iran war after the US midterm elections, with a tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz highlighting supply risk. Brent for December rose 2.5% to $117.75 and WTI rose 2.7% to $104.79. Analysts cite doubts about a viable diplomatic path and expected US and allied escalation.

Gold fell 3.1% to $3,897.09 an ounce. Silver, platinum and palladium slid into technically oversold territory as the stock selloff pulled metals down with it. Canada's TSX materials sector fell 4.84%.

Exxon and Chevron beat profit forecasts as refining margins surged. Exxon earned more from refining than from exploration and drilling for the first time in at least six years. Chevron's downstream earnings hit a six-year high. The report ties this to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on refineries in Saudi Arabia and Russia.

Reddit fell 28.70% after warning that Google's AI search is cutting referral traffic. It said daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter if referrals keep declining.

Other results: FedEx Freight rose 14.13% after beating estimates and guiding fourth-quarter profit above estimates. Capri raised annual revenue and profit forecasts. General Dynamics raised 2026 forecasts on record backlog. AbbVie raised its annual profit forecast on Skyrizi and Rinvoq demand and trades at record highs, up about 27% this year.

Apple, Palantir, Diamondback, Estee Lauder, Marriott, ON Semiconductor, Progressive, Vertex and others report today. Apple is the main event, with new CEO John Ternus expected to face questions on the holiday outlook, AI plans and screen issues with the new foldable iPhone. Palantir is expected to show about 85% revenue growth.

Today's data: ISM manufacturing PMI for October is expected at 54.7 versus 54.5 prior. Construction spending for September is expected at +0.3% month on month versus +0.9%. S&P Global's final manufacturing PMI was 56 in the prior reading.

Friday's October jobs report is the key data event of the week. Payrolls are expected at +65,000 versus +29,000 prior, unemployment at 4.2%, average hourly earnings at +0.3% month on month and +2.9% year on year versus 3.0%. ADP is expected at 65,000 on Wednesday and JOLTS at 7.100 million on Tuesday.

Third-quarter Employment Cost Index rose 0.8% after 0.9% in the second quarter, in line with expectations. Wages and salaries rose 0.7% and were up 3.1% over 12 months, mostly lagging inflation. The report reads this as the labor market not being an inflation risk.

Fed backdrop: a separate item says new data may challenge Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's view that the economy can handle a robust expansion without stoking inflation, as a key price-pressure measure jumped and growth ran beyond what most officials see as sustainable. Three Fed officials made the case for more rate increases after the meeting that left rates steady. Several Fed speakers are scheduled Thursday and Friday (Hammack, Barkin, Logan, Williams, Musalem, Bowman).

US fiscal deterioration is a main investor concern into the midterms. The national debt tops $40 trillion and deficits point to heavier issuance. A Wealthspire strategist said a Democratic win would not necessarily change Treasury's financing strategy.

Digital assets: hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in a heist analysts blame on North Korea, described as potentially the largest financial heist of all time. No price impact is described in the report.

Consumer: NIQ data show Halloween chocolate sales fell $33.1 million in the nine weeks ending October 17 versus a year earlier, the biggest drop in at least three years. US consumer sentiment is near a record low. Hershey and Mondelez face cost-of-living and health-conscious shoppers.

Canada: the TSX fell 1.74%. Statistics Canada's advance estimate points to a 0.1% GDP contraction in September after August stalled, and third-quarter annualized growth of 1.3% versus the Bank of Canada's 2% projection. An Edward Jones strategist said this suggests the BoC should be cautious about raising rates. PM Carney said the EU and Canada will define an 'associate member' partnership by mid-2027.

Data quality: the report gives two different closes for several stocks. Intel is $64.62 (-29.81%) in the table versus $65.76 (-28.58%) in the text. Reddit is $92.30 versus $92.40, FedEx Freight is $125.42 versus $125.19, and spot gold is $3,884.75 versus $3,897.09. Capri's close is printed as '$xx'. The market data appears to be for the prior Friday session.

Other items: the UK CMA opened an investigation into Meta's terms for publishers and advertisers, and the terms planned for November 20 are on hold. Oregon's Supreme Court hears arguments Tuesday on reviving a wildfire class action against Berkshire-owned PacifiCorp. Imperial Oil is considering an earlier decision on its Aspen oil sands project (up to 150,000 barrels of bitumen per day).

market_movers.rationale: Intel guided quarterly revenue more than $1 billion below estimates and expects no positive cash flow this year. Shares fell 28.58% to $65.76 in the text, its worst day ever.
Reddit warned Google's AI search is cutting referral traffic and daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter. Shares fell 28.70%.
Illumina fell 18.21% to $237.24 in the S&P 500 losers table. The report gives no reason.

FedEx Freight beat third-quarter adjusted profit and revenue estimates and guided fourth-quarter profit above estimates. Evercore ISI and Jefferies said its medium-term targets are becoming more achievable. Shares rose 14.13% to $125.19.
Regeneron rose 13.55% to $929.68 in the S&P 500 gainers table. The report gives no reason.
Global Payments rose 12.30% to $96.26 in the S&P 500 gainers table. The report gives no reason.

Capri raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $3.42 billion (versus $3.40 billion earlier and $3.41 billion LSEG consensus) and profit to $2.20 per share from $2.15. It expects sales to return to growth in the fourth quarter. Shares rose about 19%.
General Dynamics raised 2026 revenue and profit forecasts after a third-quarter beat. It booked nearly $99 billion in orders and a record $220.3 billion backlog on Gulfstream and submarine demand.
AbbVie beat third-quarter expectations and raised its annual profit forecast on Skyrizi and Rinvoq. Shares are up about 27% this year at record highs.
Exxon beat profit forecasts and earned more from refining than from exploration and drilling for the first time in at least six years.
Chevron beat profit forecasts and its third-quarter downstream earnings were the highest in at least six years.
Apple reports fiscal fourth-quarter results after the close today. Questions are expected on the holiday outlook, AI plans and screen issues with the new foldable iPhone.
Palantir reports after the close today with about 85% third-quarter revenue growth expected on AI-powered data analytics demand.

sector_views.rationale: The report describes a tech selloff on doubts about AI spending returns. Intel's cash-burn warning and higher hyperscaler capex are the triggers. This is the report's description of market action, not a bank's formal rating.

Exxon and Chevron beat on record refining margins linked to the Strait of Hormuz closure and refinery attacks. Oil is elevated on escalation risk. This is the report's description of results, not a bank's formal rating.
Gold fell 3.1% and silver, platinum and palladium slid into oversold territory with tech. Canada's materials index fell 4.84%.
Halloween chocolate sales fell $33.1 million year on year, the biggest drop in at least three years, on cost-of-living pressure and health-conscious buying.

earnings_insights: Intel reported fiscal third-quarter results and guided next-quarter revenue more than $1 billion below market estimates. It does not expect positive cash flow this year. These are company results and guidance, not estimates. Shares closed 28.58% lower at $65.76 in the text.

Apple reports fiscal Q4 after the close today. LSEG Smart Estimate EPS is $2.01 and the IBES EPS estimate is $1.99, versus $1.85 a year ago. Revenue estimate is $113,377.43 million. These are consensus estimates, not reported figures.

Palantir reports Q3 after the close today. EPS estimates are $0.42 (Smart Estimate) and $0.41 (IBES), versus $0.21 a year ago. Revenue estimate is $2,182.50 million, with about 85% revenue growth expected. All are estimates, not reported.

Other estimates for today (Smart Estimate EPS versus year ago, all consensus not reported): Diamondback Q3 $5.74 vs $3.08, Estee Lauder Q1 $0.52 vs $0.32, Marriott Q3 $2.86 vs $2.47, ON Semiconductor Q3 $0.88 vs $0.63, Progressive Q3 $4.15 vs $4.67, Vertex Q3 $4.77 vs $4.80, Clorox Q1 $1.11 vs $0.85. Loews has no estimate listed.

ConocoPhillips reports Thursday. LSEG consensus adjusted EPS is $2.82 versus $1.43 a year earlier. Marathon Petroleum reports Tuesday and is expected to show higher adjusted earnings on stronger refining margins. Both are estimates.
Exxon and Chevron both beat analyst profit expectations for the third quarter. Reported results, with no EPS figures in this report.

General Dynamics beat third-quarter estimates and raised 2026 revenue and profit guidance. It booked nearly $99 billion in orders including five Columbia-class and nine Virginia-class submarines. Backlog is a record $220.3 billion, more than double a year earlier, and aerospace orders were $5 billion. All reported figures.
AbbVie beat third-quarter expectations and raised its annual profit forecast. Skyrizi, Rinvoq and brain disease drugs drive growth and offset Humira declines. Reported, with no EPS figure given.

FedEx Freight posted third-quarter adjusted profit and revenue above estimates and guided fourth-quarter profit above estimates. 2027 revenue growth is guided in line with a 4%-6% medium-term target, with adjusted operating margin progressing toward 15%.

Capri guided fiscal 2027 revenue of $3.42 billion, versus $3.40 billion earlier guidance and $3.41 billion LSEG consensus. Annual profit is guided at $2.20 per share versus $2.15 earlier. Revenue is expected to return to growth in the fourth quarter.
Reddit fell 28.70% on the third-quarter report. It warned fourth-quarter daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage if referral traffic keeps declining.

Later this week: Pfizer (Tuesday, Eliquis and obesity commentary), Yum Brands, Ralph Lauren, Keurig Dr Pepper (Tuesday), CVS and McDonald's (Wednesday), Cigna, Airbnb, Tapestry, Mattel, Novavax (Thursday), Humana (Friday). Mattel faces investor calls for strategic options including a sale. Most are expected to show revenue growth, with no figures given. Bank of America and Wells Fargo executives present at a Boston conference Thursday.

crypto_views: Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a theft analysts blamed on North Korea. The report says it could be the largest financial heist of all time. No market reaction is described.
risk_factors: AI spending returns: hyperscalers raising capex while investors question the timeline for returns, with borrowing costs making debt-funded investment costlier.
Intel's warning of no positive cash flow this year and weak PC demand, which also raises concerns for the broader consumer-device supply chain as AI demand lifts memory prices.
Escalation of the Iran war after the US midterms and supply risk around the Strait of Hormuz.
US fiscal deterioration, with debt above $40 trillion and heavier issuance expected.
Inflation re-acceleration risk: a key price-pressure measure jumped and growth is above sustainable levels, with Fed officials arguing for more rate hikes.
Reddit and similar platforms losing traffic to Google's AI search answers.
Consumer weakness: sentiment near a record low and falling Halloween chocolate sales.
Legal exposure: PacifiCorp (Berkshire Hathaway) faces a possible revived class action over 2020 Oregon wildfires with potentially billions in damages.
vol_and_positioning: The Nasdaq 100 is down over 5.8% in October with more than $2 trillion of market value wiped out. Investor scrutiny of AI returns has grown.
Silver, platinum and palladium slid deep into technically oversold territory, with gold down 3.1%.
Big Tech returned the smallest share of cash to shareholders in at least 15 years, as AI spending squeezed share buybacks.
Sentiment toward tech was already fragile before Intel's report after Meta and Alphabet results showed the AI infrastructure race turning lightly indebted giants into heavy borrowers.
geopolitical: US-Israeli war with Iran: traders brace for a potential escalation after the US midterms, with an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz.
Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, with doubts about a viable diplomatic pathway, per MST Marquee and BOK Financial commentary.
Attacks on refineries in Saudi Arabia and Russia and the Russia-Ukraine war have disrupted fuel-making capacity and global energy markets.
US midterm elections approaching, with fiscal deterioration and national debt above $40 trillion cited as an investor concern.
UK CMA investigation into Meta's terms for publishers and advertisers, with Meta's planned November 20 revisions on hold.
Canada and the EU launching an 'alliance for the future', with Canada to become the EU's first 'associate member'. Germany and several other EU countries oppose the associate member term.
Binance hack of $6.3 billion blamed by analysts on North Korea.

A metals trader said the earnings pillar of the AI rally is showing cracks.
